output.name: Tamsi
output.myth: In the hungry year the herring stayed out past the reef and the boats sat on the shingle. Ennu the Kite-Wright sewed a fish from old sailcloth, stiffened it with whalebone, and hung a tin bell under its mouth. It was red as a split gull's leg, with a tail that could cut the wind. He flew it up the Lamp Road and let go. Tavo the Gale laughed and tore at the tail, but the fish held. Aun flew up beside it to hear the bell, and it rang so hard the whole coast came running. Sekúla the Sun-Kite, twelve degrees north-east on the same road, dipped her tail to them. Skeru the Asking Raven, from her stake twenty degrees north, put the question to the wind: are the herring running? The boats went out at first light, and the herring came back in silver. Hesk the Reel counts every fish. The line parted in the next gale, and the kite went up the Lamp Road for good, still ringing. When its bell sounds cold in the morning, the herring are on their way.
output.finding: Find Skeru, the Asking Raven, low in the north, then go one hand-span straight south across the sky to the red Fish Kite on the Lamp Road.
